title: Rogue remote-access campaign spread through ScreenConnect add-on, researchers say
content_md: Security researchers at Huntress said an intruder used access to multiple cloud-hosted ScreenConnect panels Wednesday to push commands to groups of managed endpoints, installing attacker-controlled copies of the remote-management software on at least 288 computers across 48 organizations. Roughly a third of the machines were reached within the first 10 minutes, and all of them within about 90 minutes, according to the company. ConnectWise, which makes ScreenConnect, said it was investigating reports of unauthorized access to certain partner ScreenConnect environments and disabled five independently developed extensions across approximately 400 partner environments wherever it could take action. The company said it had “found no evidence of a compromise of ConnectWise infrastructure or a vulnerability in ScreenConnect itself.” “Our initial assessment suggests the activity may involve a threat actor’s abuse of independent third-party extensions installed in partner environments,” the company’s advisory said. Huntress traced the activity to RMM+, one of the disabled extensions, which lets other tools manage ScreenConnect sessions without a user working through the console. The extension “bypasses ScreenConnect’s user accounts, roles, and MFA,” authenticating instead with a shared access key rather than the platform’s multifactor authentication, according to Huntress.
